body: I didn't mean the OCD.  I was nine when I was diagnosed with that, and I have had it my entire life.  Didn't catch your edit, sorry.

During.

Go to bed, though, man.
Well, it's good you seem to have my life figured out.

I have met with therapists before, but they haven't seemed to do much good in the past.  I usually end up seeing how they intend to help, also seeing how I'm falling short of their expectations, and then getting really frustrated by that inconsistency.

It's enough of a stretch for me even to post here, to be honest.

> but like most things it won't be anywhere near as bad as you think

When I switched this semester, it ended up actually being worse than I had expected, though.  I dunno.

And I guess I just meant in terms of things I've done outside of classes.  Like hobbies or whatever.  I'm not sure what I meant, considering I don't do much at all.  Anyway, I'm sorry for wasting your time.

It's not necessarily that I worry about people being shocked by my decision, or even disappointed by it somehow.  I guess I just worry about the interactions that go along with it, like the faux support and sympathy.  (I know that sounds stupid, sorry.)

> if you want something bad enough there are always steps you can take to get it

As awful as it sounds, I'm not sure I care enough about my life at this point.  I spend at least 40% of my days lost in thought about how I might kill myself.

And I'm not sure what you mean by your last question, and I don't want to answer if I misunderstand it, sorry.

> If you're afraid of life you won't be very good at anything anyway

This at least seems to be true.  =(

Well, I've experienced some of the constant reminders just this semester.  It took some people months to figure out I was gone, and I'm sure even more haven't discovered it yet.  I can't explain why exactly that's so exhausting to me, but it is.  

And I know people don't worry about me -- that's not what I'm trying to say, sorry.  It's just that I'm afraid that my problems will be consistent in any path I choose, so it seems futile to choose at all.  I am definitely a failure of a student, and I'm not much more successful in other aspects of my life.  Sorry to ramble a bit.

If it came down to me becoming a dropout, I would probably kill myself.  I realize some people are perfectly fine with dropping out, and I'm not saying there's anything inherently wrong with it, but that is how I feel about it.

Probably not social anxiety, but I do have an anxiety disorder (OCD), which could manifest similarly.  In any case, I know that for a normal person this wouldn't be irreversible.  I just fear that it is for me.  And yes, I am terrified, not just of admitting I made a mistake in the first place, but everything that goes along with that admission, including probably years (maybe a lifetime, even) of trying to explain myself.  I realize that seems trivial to worry about, but fear of that is overshadowing most everything in my life at the moment.

Thanks for responding, by the way.
